cards.explanation: The answer is to catch Jesus in His words (Mark 12:13). Pharisees, strict keepers of the law, and Herodians, who backed Herod's family, showed up with a question meant to catch Him. It's like a coworker saying "Be honest, what do you think of the new schedule?" with the boss standing right behind you.

The answer is whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar. They asked, "Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?" (Mark 12:14). Caesar was the Roman emperor, so it's a loaded question about money and power. All that praise was the warm-up lap before the real question.

The answer is False. Mark 12:15 says Jesus "…saw through their hypocrisy…" and asked, "Why are you testing Me?" They laid on the compliments, but He saw what was under them. I've had folks butter me up before, and I always check my pockets.

The answer is that He asks whose image and inscription are on the coin. He asked, "Whose image is this? And whose inscription?" (Mark 12:16). He doesn't need a lecture, just a coin and two simple questions. Sometimes the best answer is already sitting in your pocket.
The answer is "Caesar’s," they answered (Mark 12:16). Even the men setting the trap had to say it out loud. Their own answer set up what Jesus said next.

The answer is that Jesus says to give Caesar what is Caesar's and God what is God's. He said, "Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s." (Mark 12:17). No yes, no no, just one answer that covered both. The coin they brought had Caesar's image and inscription on it (Mark 12:16), and I've never seen a loaded question answered so calmly.

The answer is True. Mark 12:17 says they "…marveled at Him." They were sent to catch Jesus in His words (Mark 12:13), and they marveled at Him instead. I think that's the last reaction they planned on.

The answer is that the second brother marries the widow. "Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children." (Mark 12:21). That fits the rule the Sadducees say Moses wrote: if a man's brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother's widow (Mark 12:19). The Sadducees are building their story one brother at a time.

The answer is True, that's how the Sadducees tell it. "In this way, none of the seven left any children." (Mark 12:22). That's the whole setup for their big question. Seven brothers and not one little footprint in the flour.

The answer is whose wife she will be in the resurrection. The Sadducees ask, "In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her." (Mark 12:23). The Sadducees don't believe in the resurrection, so I think they were hoping the puzzle would knock it over. That's a lot of husbands for one question.

The answer is the Scriptures and the power of God. Jesus says, "Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?" (Mark 12:24). Two things, and He names both in one question. The Scriptures and the power of God are what the Sadducees were missing.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven." (Mark 12:25). So the Sadducees' question about whose wife she'd be doesn't work the way they thought. No wedding, no problem.

The answer is the burning bush. Jesus asks, "…have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses…" (Mark 12:26). God told Moses there, "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob…" (Mark 12:26; Exodus 3:6).

The answer is "living." Jesus says, "He is not the God of the dead, but of the living." (Mark 12:27). He gets there from what God told Moses at the burning bush: "I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob…" (Mark 12:26; Exodus 3:6). That's Jesus answering the Sadducees from the Book of Moses.

The answer is which commandment is the most important. The scribe asks, "Which commandment is the most important of all?" (Mark 12:28). A scribe is a teacher of the law, so this is his home turf. I think he'd been listening closely, since he noticed how well Jesus had answered them (Mark 12:28).

The answer is to love the Lord your God with everything. Jesus says, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength." (Mark 12:30). First comes who God is, then comes loving Him. And He says it's the most important of all.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "No other commandment is greater than these." (Mark 12:31). He gave the scribe two: love the Lord your God, and love your neighbor as yourself. Nothing bigger is hiding in the back of the cupboard.

The answer is all burnt offerings and sacrifices. The scribe says loving God and loving your neighbor "…is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices." (Mark 12:33). He puts that love above all of them. That's a big thing to say out loud.

The answer is "wisely." Mark 12:34 says, "When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely, He said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”…" The scribe had just said that loving God and loving your neighbor is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices (Mark 12:33). Jesus saw that answer as wise.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "You are not far from the kingdom of God." (Mark 12:34). That's Jesus speaking to the scribe who answered wisely. After the other questioners, that's a warm word to hear.
